rv.q: This expensive import from London, based on Wilkie Collins's 1860 novel, is a musical that seems to have been conceived in a perpetual fog bank. Even when the stage is brightly lighted, you feel as if you're peering through thick gauze at characters who never quite come into focus.
Practically everyone else, unfortunately including the ever-reliable Walter Charles as Laura and Marian's crotchety uncle, tends to fade into the background.
